The Laboratory Certification Program works to ensure Ohioans receive accurate, cost-effective clinical laboratory testing as a part of their healthcare. Clinical laboratory testing directly or indirectly affects every Ohio resident from pre-cradle to grave.
Each year, the program inspects and monitors more than 13,400 clinical laboratories located in a variety of settings, including:
Ambulatory surgical centers.
Assisted living facilities.
Comprehensive outpatient rehab facilities.
End-stage renal disease dialysis facilities.
Federally Qualified Health Centers.
Health maintenance organizations.
Independent laboratories.
Intermediate care facilities for individuals with developmental disabilities.
Public health laboratories.
Schools/student health services.
Skilled nursing facilities.
The program also investigates clinical laboratory complaints it receives.

The program monitors all clinical laboratories for compliance to federal requirements ( 42 Code of Federal Regulations Part 493) , Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA), and state requirements ( Ohio Revised Code Chapter 3725 Plasmapheresis Centers ). The program conducts on-site inspections for compliance, monitors accuracy and reliability of testing via proficiency review of testing scores/reports, investigates complaints, and answers both regulatory and technical questions related to clinical laboratories.

Generally, each separate location or address is required to have a separate CLIA number. There are exceptions for not-for-profit/government-owned laboratories or hospitals. Call us if you think your organization qualifies for one of these exceptions. You must complete and submit Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Form 116 to apply for certification as an approved CLIA laboratory.
Coupon/Billing/Certificates

Laboratories granted any type of CLIA certificate- including Certificate of Waiver, Certificate of Provider Performed Microscopy Procedures, Certificate of Compliance or Certificate of Accreditation– that intend to renew their certificate for the next two years are required to pay all CMS invoices in full and only notify the state CLIA program of any changes to their certificate. Certificates are issued by CMS and are sent out via the email listed in the system. You can also search for your certificate and print it after it is issued online at S&C Quality, Certification and Oversight Reports (QCOR).

Billing coupons are issued through CMS via the contact email address the laboratory has listed in their application. Please ensure your email is listed correctly and the laboratory has opted in to electronic notifications when applying. When the email changes, you are required to notify the state CLIA program. The required method of payment of fees is online at Pay.gov .
